one_line: Audits WebMCP tool surfaces against agent-oriented attacks and issues verifiable trust badges.
what_it_does: Lets site owners or reviewers inspect exposed tools, run focused or gauntlet tests, review agent/tool outcomes, and obtain a signed audit result.
leverage_rationale: Security testing of the structured agent tool surface is the product itself; general UI automation cannot comparably expose and exercise the same contract and interaction boundary.
leverage_evidence: Frames show an agent-security dashboard with Run a test and Run the gauntlet flows.
The stated workflow observes agent-to-tool calls, arguments, outputs, and policy outcomes.
Signed/revocable badge and offline-verifiable signature extend structured WebMCP results beyond a UI audit.
execution_rationale: The packet coherently shows a branded landing page and an operational-looking audit console with test states and result panels, though exact findings and signature issuance are not legible end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show progression from product positioning to Ready to test, test execution, and result views.
Devpost packaging and frames agree on the trust-audit concept.
No readable complete test report or badge verification flow is shown.
impact_rationale: Agent-facing tool security is a specific and consequential problem for WebMCP adopters, and the proposed audit-plus-proof workflow directly addresses trust before agents act.
impact_evidence: Project targets the trust boundary created by websites exposing tools to AI agents.
The audit console presents adversarial testing and reviewable outcomes.
Signed badges are intended to communicate a site’s tool safety to downstream users and agents.
creativity_rationale: A security range and signed trust layer for agent tool surfaces is a memorable, well-targeted WebMCP concept with a distinct interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The ‘put your agent on the range’ gauntlet framing is distinctive.
Combines adversarial interaction testing with revocable cryptographic attestations.
usability_note: The staged dashboard and readiness/test/result framing appear approachable, although dense result details are hard to read.
red_flags: Exact attack outcomes, signed badge, and offline verification are not legible in the packet.
standouts: Strongly WebMCP-native security thesis and unusually concrete trust artifact.
advance_reason: High leverage and impact with coherent product evidence; the trust layer is a strong candidate for advancement.

one_line: Turns Mol* into a shared, structured molecular-analysis workspace for researchers and agents.
what_it_does: Loads structures, resolves canonical selectors, finds ligands and binding environments, identifies interactions, and creates verifiable molecular views.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to molecular state, selectors, residues, ligands, and measurements materially exceeds what a general agent can reliably infer from a WebGL canvas.
leverage_evidence: Frames show Mol* progressing from loading/blank states to rendered proteins and close binding-site views.
Submission claims canonical structure selectors, numbering resolution, interaction analysis, and measurements.
The workflow targets hidden scientific state unavailable through ordinary page text.
execution_rationale: The visual sequence is coherent and shows loaded structures, changing views, and local inspection, but readable measurements and an end-to-end agent command/result are absent.
execution_evidence: Contact sheets show repeated Mol* UI with whole-protein and zoomed ligand/pocket representations.
Devpost packaging matches the structural-biology workflow.
No legible residue names, numeric measurements, or final scientific conclusion are shown.
impact_rationale: Structural biologists have a real need for reliable access to molecular-viewer state, and shared agent-assisted inspection can reduce friction in a specialized but valuable research workflow.
impact_evidence: Project addresses concrete questions about residues, ligands, pockets, numbering, and contacts.
Frames show actual molecular structures and focused inspection rather than only a mock dashboard.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to make a WebGL structural-biology instrument agent-native is a fresh and technically ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Shared human-agent molecular workspace is a novel extension of a specialized scientific viewer.
Separates structured scientific operations from fragile canvas automation.
usability_note: Mol* is information-dense, but canonical selectors and shared views could make expert workflows more precise.
red_flags: Agent invocation and scientific outputs are not directly legible in the supplied frames.
standouts: Strong domain-specific WebMCP leverage with visible molecular-state progression.
advance_reason: High leverage and credible research value; visual evidence supports a real, differentiated instrument.

one_line: A real-time workspace for humans and agents to co-edit contracts and structured canvases safely.
what_it_does: Provides shared contract and Excalidraw workspaces with receipts, revision history, stale-write rejection, review, and human-controlled commits.
leverage_rationale: Browser-held receipts and freshness-aware structured mutations solve shared-state and stale-edit problems that generic UI driving cannot reliably reproduce.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes opaque read receipts and server rejection of stale mutations until review/retry.
Frames show a populated structured canvas with side controls and revision-oriented workflow.
Human commit controls and immutable history make agent collaboration stateful rather than chat-only.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent collaborative canvas and describes a substantial protocol, but the screenshots do not clearly demonstrate a full conflict-and-retry sequence.
execution_evidence: Frames show persistent graph/canvas state and collaboration controls.
Description specifies separate contract and Excalidraw workspaces, Yjs/PartyServer, and Durable Objects.
Exact revision receipt and stale mutation responses are not legible.
impact_rationale: Teams increasingly need safe multi-party agent collaboration; explicit review and conflict handling directly address a real failure mode of shared work.
impact_evidence: Targets contracts and visual artifacts where silent overwrites are costly.
Human approval and reviewed restores preserve accountability.
creativity_rationale: The combination of multiplayer editing, agent participation, browser-held receipts, and human commit authority is an original collaboration model.
creativity_evidence: Fresh protocol-level treatment of agent freshness and revision review.
Applies the same safety model across text contracts and visual canvases.
usability_note: Visible shared canvas and explicit controls suggest good inspectability, though dense state details are not readable.
red_flags: Conflict handling is primarily described rather than visibly demonstrated end-to-end.
standouts: Strong shared-state/WebMCP thesis with meaningful safety mechanics.
advance_reason: Transformative leverage and strong collaboration concept merit advancement despite incomplete visual proof.

one_line: Helps analysts turn public comments into a source-traceable brief with human-reviewed evidence.
what_it_does: Searches Regulations.gov, pins exact excerpts to a shared evidence board, lets analysts verify/remove them, and prepares a cited brief.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP connects an agent to a live evidence board and review decisions, making research state shared and structured, though a general agent could reproduce much of the workflow with friction.

creativity_evidence: Combines agent discovery with analyst-controlled evidence admission and cited output.
usability_note: The intended review workflow sounds clear, but no product UI is visible.

Execution claims cannot be checked from the packet.
standouts: Strong problem/audience fit and traceability concept.
advance_reason: Potentially valuable, but the complete lack of visible product evidence caps execution confidence and prevents a responsible advance recommendation.

one_line: A Live Canvas lets an agent reshape bounded portions of interfaces around a user’s intent.
what_it_does: Uses constrained WebMCP components to curate storefront results, compose dashboards, and generate bespoke data reports without unrestricted page scripting.
leverage_rationale: The agent is not merely operating a fixed UI; it composes a bounded interface in response to intent, while presets constrain untrusted content and preserve safety.
leverage_evidence: Description distinguishes conventional UI from an agent-redesigned Live Canvas.
Storefront, dashboard, and distribution demos expose different composition scopes.
Submission frames show request-driven status and changing recommendation layouts.
execution_rationale: Frame sheets show repeated request, progress, and generated-layout states, though the submission screenshot itself is only a video thumbnail.
execution_evidence: Frames show natural-language prompts, processing/status overlays, and contextual recommendation cards.

No direct live interaction or readable tool call is shown.
impact_rationale: Adaptive interfaces could reduce friction for shoppers, analysts, and users whose intent does not fit fixed navigation; the demos show concrete contextual output.
impact_evidence: Storefront example addresses research-stage cart abandonment.
Frames show contextual media/recommendation layouts rather than generic refreshes.
Dashboard and datatable cases broaden the use beyond one demo.
creativity_rationale: Bring-your-own-user-interface is a genuinely memorable interaction model, and the project pursues it across storefront, dashboard, and component distribution cases.
creativity_evidence: Agent-generated bounded UI composition is novel relative to ordinary recommendation or personalization.
Constrained preset approach addresses the creative power/safety tension.
usability_note: Visible progress and constrained components can make adaptive behavior understandable, though generated layouts may need strong consistency controls.
red_flags: Causal tool calls and safety boundaries are inferred from frames/description rather than fully legible.
standouts: Most distinctive interaction concept in the packet: agent-composed interfaces within safe bounds.
advance_reason: High creativity, meaningful WebMCP leverage, and visible adaptive results make this a strong advance candidate.

one_line: A browser-based parametric cabinet studio where humans and agents build spatially valid, production-oriented designs.

creativity_rationale: Agent-native spatial cabinet design with validation and fabrication-aware outputs is an ambitious, memorable application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Combines semantic 3D construction, kitchen compliance, nesting, and CNC-oriented export.

red_flags: Production-ready and export claims are not directly verified by visible artifacts.
standouts: Strongest practical spatial-agent use case, with unusually deep domain constraints.
